Kincaid (17 targets, 263 yards, 218 air yards, 15.5 yards/target) is the receiving weapon aimed at the middle, where NE allows 10.53 YPA. Moore's 285 air yards want explosives NE has mostly not given up (5/99).

edge_players.edge_sentence: Cook is at 115.3 rush yards a game on 58 carries over three weeks, and NE is allowing 4.41 YPC, so 86.5 is light if BUF leads and keeps the lead-back role he has already shown.
edge_players.must_be_true: Cook stays healthy — no injury note in the pack — and keeps something near a 19-carry share in a game BUF is not chasing.
edge_players.kills_it: A pass-heavy chase, a late scratch, or efficiency falling to NE's 4.41 YPC on only 15-17 carries (about 66-75 yards) instead of the 6.0 he has posted.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Kincaid is averaging 87.7 receiving yards on 17 targets and NE is leaking the middle at 10.53 YPA, so 48.5 is a low bar even if a BUF lead shortens the passing game.
edge_players.must_be_true: Kincaid keeps a full route share and still sees a slice of the middle targets (about 5.7 per game in the L3), with Allen functional vs NE's 41% blitz.
edge_players.kills_it: A first-half blowout that parks the passing game, or NE taking the TE away so Knox (4 targets, 17 yards) and Shakir eat the leftovers and Kincaid stalls in the 20s.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so nothing can be sized to a sharp price and any implied win rate above 70% would be untrustworthy anyway. Pack form agrees with Kincaid (87.7 vs a 48.5 line; middle 10.53 YPA). It only partly agrees with the strong Cook read: 115.3 vs 86.5 looks easy, but haircutting him to the yards NE actually allows is 19.3 carries times 4.41 YPC = about 85, a miss, and without game logs the 346 yards may be one spike. That disagreement flags Cook for the human; it does not cut him. Kincaid stays a lean, not a model-confirmed strong.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because Cook's 6.0 YPC was the fluke the missing game logs would have shown, BUF was in a tighter game than the form script, and 17 carries at 4.2 YPC finished near 71, under 86.5, while the passing game went to Moore's air yards instead of a grind. The other way around also loses the slip: BUF led big by half, Cook cleared, but Kincaid saw two targets before Allen was closed and finished under 48.5, with Knox vulturing the rest. A late inactive neither of us could see would zero either leg. The efficiency counter-case on Cook is stronger than the raw 115-yard average, which is why the leg is flagged rather than sized; Kincaid's number is softer but dies in a laugher.
slip_story: One script only: BUF controls but does not bury NE by halftime, so Cook is the clock against a 4.41 YPC run defense and Kincaid still clears a depressed 48.5 through the middle leak. Do not add NE rush overs (Stevenson 32.5, Henderson 40.5, Maye 27.5), do not add Allen rush over 31.5 (a blowout helps Cook and sits Allen's legs), and do not mix in a total under. No TDs, no receptions, one market per player.
